subject.title: doctor --fix crashes on 'prepared model runtime publication timed out' before persisting config migrations

question: Should doctor persist finalized legacy-config migrations before later runtime-preparation checks, while preserving a visible warning for the prepared-runtime publication timeout?
rationale: The report identifies a bounded ordering bug, but maintainers must confirm the intended error policy for prepared-runtime publication rather than broadly suppressing lifecycle failures.

options.title: Persist migrations first and warn
options.body: Write the validated doctor migration result as soon as config finalization completes, then retain the prepared-runtime timeout as a visible nonfatal warning when model resolution is unavailable.

options.title: Keep publication fatal
options.body: Retain the existing fatal runtime-publication behavior but move all config persistence ahead of it so valid migrations are not discarded.

recommendation.title: Persist migrations first and warn
recommendation.body: Write the validated doctor migration result as soon as config finalization completes, then retain the prepared-runtime timeout as a visible nonfatal warning when model resolution is unavailable.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent merged work connects this contributor to both the model-runtime lifecycle and doctor-owned config migration surfaces.
